notes: Route: Arc XP by-day sitemaps on the R7 section hosts, not www.r7.com. www.r7.com's daily sitemaps list only /tudo-do-r7/*, /todos-os-videos/* and /validacao/* paths and its robots.txt line 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /tudo-do-r7/*' (fetched 2026-10-25, md5 a6989cdb..., stable over 3 fetches) makes polite_fetch refuse every one of them (that is why the previous attempt scored 0/6: status -1, 0 chars on https://www.r7.com/tudo-do-r7/...-DDMMYYYY/). The same Arc feeds are served by noticias., esportes., entretenimento. and record.r7.com, whose articles sit on section paths (/brasil/, /eleicoes/2026/, /famosos-e-tv/, /lance/ ...) that their own robots.txt allows for User-agent: *. Script: for each host fetch /arc/outboundfeeds/sitemap-index-byday/ (day -> /arc/outboundfeeds/sitemap{,2,3...}/YYYY-MM-DD/), fetch the 31 day sitemaps in the window, keep the <loc> article URLs, drop /video/, /fotos/, /galeria/, /ao-vivo/ stubs, take the date from the trailing ddmmyyyy in the slug (the site's own statement of the local America/Sao_Paulo publication day; <lastmod> equals the page's article:published_time), drop slug dates outside 2026-09-25..2026-10-25 (evergreen pages are re-listed in later day sitemaps), fall back to the sitemap's day only when a slug carries no date, and re-check every candidate against the host's live robots rules via polite_fetch.robots_for before writing, so each written URL is fetchable. 12528 unique URLs, 31 days, per-day 222-547; 2026-09-30=524, 2026-10-10=224, 2026-10-20=524. Verified 20 random rows re-fetched: all HTTP 200, 13.5k-22.7k chars of text, page datePublished equal to the listed date in 20/20. Runtime 4m08s (1 index + 31 day sitemaps per host, all through polite_fetch at its per-host rate).
